key_insight: Synthetic data help only when they add target-relevant coverage without introducing training errors that outweigh their benefit, and their value changes as the training set grows.
engineering_relevance: For LLM fine-tuning, the paper gives a principled way to choose which synthetic examples to add so selection budgets are spent on examples most likely to improve downstream task performance.
method: Derive a linear theory for the marginal value of synthetic examples during training.
Define Training-Aware Target Coverage (TATC) to pick candidates with beneficial training effects.
Select examples that expand coverage of target-relevant directions already underrepresented in the available data.
evidence_signal: Experiments on text and image data validate the linear theory, and on GSM8K TATC improves Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B-Instruct over alternative synthetic-data selection methods across selection budgets.
watch_item: The method depends on the assumptions of the linear theory, so performance may shift when training dynamics or synthetic error patterns depart from that regime.
paper_title: Training-Aware Target Coverage for Synthetic Data Selection
